story.head: A natural hat trick for Thompson
paras: This one got way too interesting for the Sabres. There were six goals in the first period alone. Mikael Granlund and Cutter Gauthier scored power-play goals 57 seconds apart early in the period to put the Ducks up 2-0. Tyson Kozak got the Sabres on the board midway through the period. Roger McQueen, in his eighth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Sam Colangelo, 35 seconds later to make it 3-1 for the Ducks. Noah Östlund and Tage Thompson scored just under four minutes apart later in the period to tie it 3-3. Thompson scored his second of the night late in the second to put the Sabres ahead for good. Thompson completed a natural hat trick just 15 seconds later to make it 5-3. The third period brought five goals. Jack Quinn and Zach Benson scored less than five minutes apart early in the period to make it 7-3. Gauthier scored again on the power play 49 seconds later to cut Buffalo’s lead to 7-4. Tristan Luneau and Beckett Sennecke scored 37 seconds apart with just over a minute left to make it 7-6, but the Sabres held on. Peyton Krebs assisted on all three. Two players had three-point nights: Benson with a goal and two assists, and the Ducks’ Leo Carlsson with three assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Ducks hit two posts and came up a goal short. Colten Ellis made 29 saves for the Sabres, and Ville Husso allowed seven goals on 31 shots.
The Ducks scored three power-play goals and still lost. The Sabres improved to 6-4-3, seventh in the Atlantic, while the Ducks fell to 5-7-1, fifth in the Pacific.
